own_original_text:
Executive Order 12095 November 2,1978
Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Between Wien A ir A laska, Inc.
and Certain Individuals
A  dispute exists between Wien Air Alaska, Inc., and certain individuals  
represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, a labor organization.
Section 44 o f the Airline Deregulation Act o f 1978 (Public Law 95-504)  
directed that the provisions of Section 10 o f the Railway Labor Act, as  
amended, be invoked despite the fact that the National Mediation Board has  
failed to find that the dispute in its judgment substantially threatens to inter­
rupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a section o f the  
country o f essential transportation service.
N O W , THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 44 of the  
Airline Deregulation Act o f 1978 (Public Law 95-504) it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
1-101. Establishment o f  Board. There is established a board o f three mem­
bers to be appointed by the President to investigate this dispute. No member  
of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of  
airline employees or any carrier.
1-102. Report. The board shall report its findings to the President with  
respect to the dispute within 30 days from the date o f this Order.
T he W hite  H ouse ,
Novem ber 2, 1 9 7 8 .
[FR Doc. 78-31514 Filed 11-3-78; 10:28 am]

versions.research_rationale:
EO 12095 (Creating an emergency board to investigate a dispute between Wien Air Alaska, Inc. and certain individuals), signed 1978-11-02. The order creates an emergency board for a dispute between Wien Air Alaska, Inc. and certain individuals, under Section 44 of the Airline Deregulation Act of 1978; Section 1-101 establishes a board of three members and Section 1-102 requires its report within 30 days of the date of the order. The held text has no maintaining-conditions section. First end: Section 5 of EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17, Termination of Boards, Committees, and Commissions) names this order by number, "Executive Order No. 12095," and provides that it is revoked. EO 12379 has no effective-date clause, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1982-08-17.  Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, 0 hits for this order), the eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 (0 hits) and the Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition-note search (2 hits). They are leads only; the end, the later events and the savings were decided from the held Federal Register texts named in this claim. Search of the held order texts for this order's number (the packet records a bounded number-citation search over its lookup corpus, excluding clause-draft copies): apart from the order's own copies, the matching files are EO 11022, EO 11256, EO 11829, EO 12379. The files filed under EO 11022, EO 11256 and EO 11829 matched only because they carry the same Federal Register pages as the EO 12379 revocation list; they are not separate instruments naming this order.
